name: DL-glutamic acid
aliases: glutamic acid, E, Glu, 2-aminopentanedioic acid, DL-glutaminic acid, GLU
summary: Glutamic acid (symbol Glu or E; known as glutamate in its anionic form), molecular formula C5H9NO4, is an α-amino acid that is used by almost all organisms for the biosynthesis of proteins. It is a conditionally essential amino acid, meaning that the body can generally synthesize it intrinsically, but under certain circumstances needs to procure it through food.
